_comment: Hand-written copy for week 1. The generator owns the numbers, this file owns the words. Keys under 'takes' are team ids.
headline: Dake Bates hangs 177.9 on the league
standfirst: Seventy-six point win. Highest opening number anybody in this league has ever posted. Eleven and oh against the field. Meanwhile Bingo Night survives by nine tenths of a point, Team Galakrond scores 129.6 and still goes home 0-1, and Cortisol Spyke Weeks gets a zero out of the tight end spot. Week one delivered.
lede_scores: Closest game first. See that gold border? Nine tenths of a point.
lede_rankings: One week in. Scoring does the heavy lifting, record has barely earned a vote. The color bar under each team splits its score by position.
lede_positions: Long orange, the backfield did the work. Long green, the receivers did it. Short bar, start dialing the waiver wire.

takes.8: One seventy-seven point nine. Caleb Williams goes off for 37.3. The backfield tacks on 71.7 between them. Fifty-six points clear of projection, seventy-six clear of Team evil, who drew the short straw on the schedule and paid for it. Eleven and oh against the field in all-play. Nobody in this league had a lineup that beats it. Week one, and somebody is already playing a different sport.
takes.9: Josh Allen for 35.7. Running backs pile on 63.7. On most Sundays 146.3 is your headline. Michael's Monstrous Team instead draws the third-best score in the league and beats it by seventeen anyway. Broncos defense chips in two points and nobody notices. Four quarterbacks on this roster, and the one he started went off.
takes.2: Seventy-one and a half points out of the receiver room. D'Andre Swift leads the way at 32.4. Projection said 109.6. Scoreboard said 144.6. Harrison Mevis kicks one single point and it never mattered for a second. Purdy Seconds to Mars goes down by thirty-one in a game that was decided before the late window kicked off.
takes.3: Christian Watson. Thirty-two point seven. Nobody saw that coming. CeeDeez Nutz puts 56.4 on the board from the receivers, gets fourteen more out of the kicker, and runs Cortisol Spyke Weeks off the field by 46.7. Twenty-four points clear of projection. New name, new ceiling. Fourth-highest score in the league and it was never in doubt.
takes.11: Amon-Ra St. Brown goes for 28.7. Evan McPherson goes for nineteen. Read that again. The kicker outscored the quarterback and the tight end put together. LaPorta-pottys finishes within a point and a half of projection, which is the least dramatic way there is to start 1-0, and takes down Adams and Jefferson by 14.2. Drake Maye at 9.8 and Marvin Harrison Jr. at 4.3 are Tuesday problems.
takes.6: Nine tenths of a point. Bingo Night 111.3, roadrunners 110.4. Jaylen Waddle puts up 1.2 and it was still enough. Jalen Hurts leads the way with 24.7 on a night where nothing much got going. Six and a half under projection. Fourth-lowest winning score on the board. Doesn't matter one bit. Eight receivers, one win, and the margin counts the same as seventy-six.
takes.1: Somebody call the commissioner. Team Galakrond scores 129.6, third best in the entire league, goes 7-4 against the field in all-play, and walks off 0-1. Kenneth Walker rips off 34.1. The backfield produces 66.2. All of it wasted on the one team that scored more. Sitting seventh because record still gets a vote in week one. That won't last.
takes.7: Bijan Robinson takes care of business with 31.3. Trey McBride adds 24.5 from the tight end spot. Then the receivers turn in thirteen points. Thirteen. For the week. Add a Texans defense that finished at minus four, an actual negative number in an actual starting lineup, and 113.7 never had a prayer against 144.6. Right on projection too. That's the part that stings.
takes.10: Loses by nine tenths of a point with a zero at tight end. Colston Loveland: no catches, no yards, no points, in a game decided by less than one. David Montgomery does his job with 28.9. That 110.4 beats four other teams on this slate. The roadrunners drafted with conviction back in August. Week one was not kind about it.
takes.12: Dallas Goedert for 23.7, and that is the whole highlight reel. Team evil comes in nineteen and a half under projection, gets a goose egg out of the Chargers defense, and runs straight into the 177.9 buzzsaw. Seventy-six point loss, biggest margin of the week by a mile. Christian McCaffrey anchors this roster and it put up 102.0. That does not hold.
takes.5: Justin Jefferson does his part with 31.2. Matthew Stafford does not. Four point one. That is the entire quarterback output for the week, from the guy everybody agreed was the steal of draft night. Adams and Jefferson finishes twenty-one under projection and drops one by 14.2. The roster is still good. The timing was brutal.
takes.4: Ninety-two points. Kyle Pitts: zero. Tight end position, total: zero. Twenty-seven under projection, lowest score in the league, beaten by 46.7 in a game that was over by Sunday afternoon. Derrick Henry goes for 35.3 and carries this thing on his back. Tells you everything you need to know about the other eight spots.
